<p>
        The Papercusp specification defines four core roles. <strong>Which
        of these are required depends on the install's declared shape</strong>
        (see §4.1) — the most common shape (`iterative`) requires
        all four; specialized shapes can opt out. Plugins may register
        additional roles regardless of shape.
      </p>

      <table>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>Role</th>
            <th>When invoked</th>
            <th>Reads</th>
            <th>Writes</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Planner</strong></td>
            <td>Once, at install activation; or when the goal materially changes</td>
            <td>`goals`, install spec</td>
            <td>`tasks` (initial breakdown), `validation_contract`</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td colspan="4"><em>Implementation note: in the shipped Papercup pipeline the
            single "Planner" role above is realized as two roles — <strong>Scoper</strong>
            (scope + acceptance) followed by <strong>Architect</strong> (technical
            breakdown). The canonical role ids live in <code>AGENT_ROLES</code>
            (<code>packages/agent-mcp/src/role-config.ts</code>), where the registry
            list order is scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer →
            debugger → documenter → curator. That list order is <strong>not</strong>
            the dispatch pipeline: the executable per-feature spine lives in the
            <code>coding-factory</code> blueprint
            (<code>libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml</code>),
            and runs <strong>scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer →
            documenter → curator</strong> — with <code>debugger</code> excluded from
            the spine. (The <code>coding</code> id was reused by the 2026-06-18 rename
            for the Pot/Mug blueprint — <code>kind: pot</code>, only
            <code>DONE</code>/<code>ESCALATE</code>/<code>IDLE</code> edges — so it
            carries no scoper→…→curator spine; look at <code>coding-factory</code>,
            not <code>coding</code>, for the pipeline.) Two refinements the registry
            order hides: <code>reviewer</code> is not a per-feature director verb but
            a PR-boundary <strong>approval gate</strong> (<code>gates.approvals</code>),
            so the verbs that actually dispatch are scoper/architect/worker/validator/documenter/curator;
            and <code>debugger</code> is a <strong>reactive overlay</strong> that fires
            read-only before a worker retry once a feature accrues
            <code>knobs.debuggerThreshold</code> failed attempts (alongside the opt-in
            <code>security-reviewer</code>/<code>crosscheck</code>/<code>ui-qa</code>
            reactive roles). The coordinator/cross-cutting role is
            <code>orchestrator</code>; <code>operator</code> and <code>oracle</code>
            are <strong>chat-surface</strong> roles, grouped separately in the registry.
            On a terminal <code>DONE</code> the finalize recipe runs
            <strong>curator → postCuratorOutputs → documenter → archive</strong> — i.e.
            curator precedes documenter, opposite of the registry list order. A
            <code>planner</code> role id exists since 2026-06-09, but it is an
            <em>interactive plan-authoring session</em> (pot-agent-tabs), not this
            spec-level Planner pipeline role. Full current registry:
            <a href="/internal/docs/harness/roles">Roles — the operational
            reference</a>.</em></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Worker</strong></td>
            <td>Every iteration with a `todo`/`failing` task</td>
            <td>`tasks`, `issues`, `worker_log`, parent goal lineage</td>
            <td>Domain output (code/text/etc.) + status update on the task</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Validator</strong></td>
            <td>Every iteration with a `validating` task</td>
            <td>`validation_contract`, the task's domain output, parent goal lineage</td>
            <td>`issues`, sets task status (`passed`/`failing`)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Orchestrator</strong></td>
            <td>Every tick (timer-based OR event-triggered)</td>
            <td>All of the above + `pending_events`</td>
            <td>One decision verb (above)</td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <p>
        Roles are defined by <strong>prompt files</strong>, not code. Improvements compound without a deploy, branches are mergeable, and the cache key (the prompt content) is stable for a given role-version.
      </p>

      

### 4.1 Install shapes — which roles a given install must implement



      <p>
        <em>Design spec — not yet implemented as written.</em> The shipped substrate
        configures harnesses through <strong>blueprints</strong> (see
        <code>blueprint:create</code> / <code>blueprint:catalog</code> and the
        <code>@papercusp/orchestrator/blueprint</code> package), which declare their
        roles, spine model, triggers, and dispatch policy directly (per-role model
        selection rides the role-level <code>model</code> field / <code>knobs.models</code>,
        not a blueprint-level tier). There is no
        <code>defineManifest</code> helper and no <code>shape</code> enum
        (<code>iterative</code>/<code>scheduled</code>/<code>reactive</code>/<code>passive</code>)
        in code today; the section below is the original role-requirement design.
      </p>

      <p>
        Not every install runs an iterative plan-then-build loop. A pure
        scheduling install (cron + alerting, no goals) has no use for a
        planner or validator — forcing it to ship no-op stubs invites
        copy-paste smell. The install's `shape` in its manifest
        determines which roles are required:
      </p>

      <table>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>Shape</th>
            <th>Required roles</th>
            <th>Use case</th>
            <th>Examples</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>`iterative`</strong> (default)</td>
            <td>planner + worker + validator + orchestrator</td>
            <td>Goal-driven work that breaks down into validated tasks. The historical Papercusp shape.</td>
            <td>Papercup, sheets-clone, habit-tracker, any product-build install</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>`scheduled`</strong></td>
            <td>worker + orchestrator</td>
            <td>Recurring or routine-driven work without explicit goal/task decomposition. Plan and validation aren't applicable.</td>
            <td>weekly-briefings, daily-cost-report, nightly-backup</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>`reactive`</strong></td>
            <td>orchestrator only</td>
            <td>Pure event-handling — orchestrator dispatches plugin-defined roles in response to `pending_events`. No first-party worker.</td>
            <td>webhook-router, slack-bot, on-call-escalator</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>`passive`</strong></td>
            <td>none (zero roles)</td>
            <td>Pure consumer — listens to hooks, contributes UI surface, queries other plugins' data via `data:read:*` capabilities, but never invokes an LLM. No prompts to author. Schema may still be declared (for the plugin's own storage).</td>
            <td>dashboard-widgets, status-monitors, audit-loggers, read-only reports</td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <p>
        Why `passive` matters: dashboard widgets and observability
        plugins shouldn't be forced to ship even a `worker` stub.
        A passive install can register hooks, contribute UI, declare its own
        schema, and read other plugins' data — all without paying any LLM
        budget or implementing role prompts. Most "extension" plugins (those
        that augment, rather than build) belong in this shape.
      </p>

      ```typescript
// In an install's manifest:
export default defineManifest({
  name: 'weekly-briefings',
  shape: 'scheduled',                      // → only requires worker + orchestrator
  // planner/validator omitted; substrate doesn't error
  capabilities: ['routines:write', 'http:fetch:slack.com'],
  routines: [{ name: 'weekly-summary', trigger: { kind: 'cron', expr: '0 9 * * MON' } }],
});
```

      <p>
        The substrate validates the shape contract at install time — a
        `scheduled` install that ships only an orchestrator is
        rejected with a clear error pointing at the missing worker. A
        `reactive` install that ships a worker is accepted (extra
        roles are always fine; missing required ones are not).
      </p>

      <p>
        Authors writing a new install pick the most restrictive shape that
        fits — it keeps the contract honest and saves them from writing
        no-op prompts. The default is `iterative` for backward
        compatibility with installs that pre-date this section.
      </p>
